# roadstyle

> Python library: turn a GeoDataFrame of road edges (LineString geometry + an OSM `highway` column) into one styled, interactive, offline HTML map (MapLibre, data inlined) with road cartography (casing and fill, per-zoom widths, labels, one-way arrows, bridges and tunnels, 3D), Google Street View for the clicked road (a popup link by default, `street_view="window"` for a floating window, `rs.render_street_view` for a side-by-side page), and a `window.rs*` JavaScript API. `pip install roadstyle`; main call `rs.render_edges(gdf, ...).save("map.html")`.

Edges are directed: a two-way road is two edges with reversed geometry. JS calls (rsSelect, rsColor, rsFocus) take roadstyle feature ids from `rsQuery`, never your own `edge_id`. Unknown keywords to `render_edges` are silently ignored.

- [Agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Khoshkhah/roadstyle/main/skills/roadstyle/SKILL.md): the one call, the data contract, the JS API and the traps, in one page

- [Parameters & API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Khoshkhah/roadstyle/main/docs/parameters.md): every public function and class, every keyword of render_edges (per backend), StyleConfig, Overlay
- [Web backend & JS API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Khoshkhah/roadstyle/main/docs/web-backend.md): grade separation, 3D, vector tiles, color_options, overlays, the JavaScript API and events
- [Palettes, base maps & settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Khoshkhah/roadstyle/main/docs/palettes.md): the built-in palettes, base maps and API keys, the settings override files
